# A 5 kWh battery carries *80% of summer evenings*; doubling it adds 9 points for 3,700 € more.

What size of battery to add to a 6 kW rooftop array on a four-person house, from an installer's quote and a year of meter readings.

Illustrative numbers, not a real quote

<h2 data-nav="System">The battery sits behind the inverter</h2>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
	panels["Roof panels, 6 kW"] --> inverter["Hybrid inverter"]
	inverter --> house["House"]
	inverter -->|"surplus"| battery["Battery"]
	battery -->|"evening"| inverter
	grid["Grid"] -->|"shortfall"| house
```

- The <span data-ref="panels">panels</span> stay as they are.
- The <span data-ref="inverter">hybrid inverter</span> replaces the string inverter and decides where each kWh goes.
- The <span data-ref="battery">battery</span> takes the surplus and gives it back in the evening.
- The <span data-ref="grid">grid</span> covers what is left, through a new bidirectional meter.

# How the numbers were made

A year of hourly meter readings, scaled to the quote's battery sizes with a simple charge model.

## Assumptions

| Input | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Array | 6 kW, south, 35° |
| Use | 4,920 kWh a year |
| Bought | 0.22 €/kWh |
| Sold | 0.06 €/kWh |
| Battery round trip | 90% |

## Not included

Price changes, battery wear after year ten, and any subsidy.

</View>
